Compute the meteorological data of a node at the whole-catchment scale

Source: R/plot.GRiwrmOutputsModel.R
adjustMeteoToCatchment.Rd

Replace, on a copy, the meteorological time series of a node by their area-weighted mean over the whole catchment of the node (the node and all its upstream nodes). The original object is not modified: the time series of the object passed in OutputsModel are read only.

Usage

adjustMeteoToCatchment(
  OM_id,
  id,
  OutputsModel,
  griwrm = attr(OutputsModel, "GRiwrm")
)

Arguments

OM_id

[object of class OutputsModel] the OutputsModel object of the node id (see RunModel.GRiwrmInputsModel)

id

[character] the ID of the node (See CreateGRiwrm)

OutputsModel

[object of class GRiwrmOutputsModel] the object produced by RunModel.GRiwrmInputsModel, or a list of OutputsModel objects with one item by node (names are the node IDs). When a simple list is passed, it must carry the "GRiwrm" attribute or griwrm must be provided explicitly (see below)

griwrm

[object of class GRiwrm] the network of the simulation (See CreateGRiwrm). Defaults to the "GRiwrm" attribute of OutputsModel (set by RunModel.GRiwrmInputsModel). When OutputsModel is a list which does not carry this attribute, the default resolves to NULL and griwrm must be passed explicitly, otherwise the catchment of the node cannot be identified.

Value

A copy of OM_id with the meteorological data at the whole-catchment scale.

Details

The meteorological data stored in the OutputsModel object of a node come from the meteorological data of its local sub-basin only, whereas the simulated discharge of the node integrates the flows of its whole catchment. This function computes, for each time step, the area-weighted mean of these data over the whole catchment, so that they can be used to compute statistics at the catchment scale (or displayed, see plot.GRiwrmOutputsModel).

The following time series are replaced when they are available in the OutputsModel object of the node:

  • Precip and PotEvap;

  • for a CemaNeige node, the per-layer series Temp (mean air temperature), Psol (solid precipitation) and SnowPack (snow pack state) stored in OM_id$CemaNeigeLayers, one item by elevation layer (See CreateRunOptions).

Each node contributes to the mean with its own time series weighted by the area of its local sub-basin: the part of the catchment for which the meteorological data of the node are the "real" data (See getNodeLocalArea). A node cannot contribute when its local sub-basin area is unknown or zero, or when the concerned time series is not available; a missing value in a time series excludes the node from the mean at the concerned time steps. When no node can contribute, the time series of the node id itself are returned unchanged (graceful behaviour). When the ID of the node is shared with a Diversion node (two rows of the network with the same id, see CreateGRiwrm), the local sub-basin area of the shared ID cannot be computed and the node is simply excluded from the weighted mean (graceful behaviour).

The elevation layers of the CemaNeige nodes are matched by index (layer i of a node with layer i of the other nodes) and a node with fewer layers does not contribute to the upper layer indices. The elevation of a given layer index slightly differs from one node to the other: this approximation is assumed. SnowPack is a simulated state and Psol an output of the snow module: both are adjusted as well, for the consistency of the whole-catchment display of the snow and temperature series.

The network is read from the griwrm argument, which defaults to the "GRiwrm" attribute set on the GRiwrmOutputsModel object by RunModel.GRiwrmInputsModel. When OutputsModel is a plain list without this attribute, the default resolves to NULL and griwrm must be passed explicitly.

See also

plot.GRiwrmOutputsModel(), CreateGRiwrm()

Examples

##############################################################
# Meteorological data at the catchment scale of a CemaNeige   #
# network: the network used here is a chain of 2 nodes built  #
# on the airGR example data set (L0123001)                    #
##############################################################
data(L0123001, package = "airGR")

# Network: Upstream (360 km2) -> Downstream (720 km2, i.e. a local
# sub-basin of 360 km2)
griwrm <- CreateGRiwrm(data.frame(
  id = c("Upstream", "Downstream"),
  down = c("Downstream", NA),
  length = c(0, NA),
  area = c(360, 720),
  model = rep("RunModel_CemaNeigeGR4J", 2)
))

# The 2 nodes share the meteorological data of the example data set
InputsPrecip <- matrix(BasinObs$P, ncol = 2, nrow = length(BasinObs$P))
InputsPotEvap <- matrix(BasinObs$E, ncol = 2, nrow = length(BasinObs$E))
InputsTemp <- matrix(BasinObs$T, ncol = 2, nrow = length(BasinObs$T))
InputsHypso <- matrix(rep(BasinInfo$HypsoData, 2), ncol = 2)
InputsZ <- rep(BasinInfo$HypsoData[51], 2)
colnames(InputsPrecip) <- colnames(InputsPotEvap) <- colnames(InputsTemp) <-
  colnames(InputsHypso) <- names(InputsZ) <- griwrm$id

InputsModel <- CreateInputsModel(
  griwrm,
  DatesR = BasinObs$DatesR,
  Precip = InputsPrecip,
  PotEvap = InputsPotEvap,
  TempMean = InputsTemp,
  ZInputs = InputsZ,
  HypsoData = InputsHypso
)
#> CreateInputsModel.GRiwrm: Processing sub-basin Upstream...
#> input series were successfully created on 5 elevation layers for use by CemaNeige
#> CreateInputsModel.GRiwrm: Processing sub-basin Downstream...
#> input series were successfully created on 5 elevation layers for use by CemaNeige

# Short run period (1 month) for a fast example. `Precip` and `PotEvap` are
# requested in `Outputs_Sim` because they are not part of the default
# outputs of a CemaNeige node
RunOptions <- CreateRunOptions(
  InputsModel,
  IndPeriod_Run = seq(1, 30),
  Outputs_Sim = c("DatesR", "Qsim", "CemaNeigeLayers", "Precip", "PotEvap")
)
#> model warm up period not defined: default configuration used
#>  no data were found for model warm up! No warm up period is used
#> Warning: model warm up period not defined: default configuration used
#>  no data were found for model warm up!
#> Warning: 'MeanAnSolidPrecip' not defined: it was automatically set to c(84,84,84,84,84)  from the 'InputsModel' given to the function. Be careful in case your application is (short-term) forecasting.
#> model warm up period not defined: default configuration used
#>  no data were found for model warm up! No warm up period is used
#> Warning: model warm up period not defined: default configuration used
#>  no data were found for model warm up!
#> Warning: 'MeanAnSolidPrecip' not defined: it was automatically set to c(84,84,84,84,84)  from the 'InputsModel' given to the function. Be careful in case your application is (short-term) forecasting.

# `Downstream` receives the simulated flow of `Upstream`: its parameter
# vector starts with the celerity of the routing model (airGR::RunModel_Lag)
ParamCN <- c(
  X1 = 408.774, X2 = 2.646, X3 = 131.264, X4 = 1.174,
  CNX1 = 0.962, CNX2 = 2.249
)
Param <- list(Upstream = ParamCN, Downstream = c(1, ParamCN))
OutputsModels <- RunModel(InputsModel, RunOptions = RunOptions, Param = Param)
#> RunModel.GRiwrmInputsModel: Processing sub-basin Upstream...
#> RunModel.GRiwrmInputsModel: Processing sub-basin Downstream...

# Area-weighted mean of the meteorological data over the whole catchment
# of the node `Downstream` (the local sub-basin areas are 360 km2 each, so
# the mean is the arithmetic mean of the 2 nodes here)
OutputsDownstream <- adjustMeteoToCatchment(
  OutputsModels[["Downstream"]],
  "Downstream",
  OutputsModels
)

# Precipitation at the whole-catchment scale and per-layer temperature
head(OutputsDownstream$Precip)
#> [1]  4.1 15.9  0.8  0.0  0.0  0.0
head(OutputsDownstream$CemaNeigeLayers[[1]]$Temp)
#> [1]  1.44178  1.14178  1.84395  1.44612 -0.65171  1.85263
